name: tovel
author: time-agent
description: tovel v6 - ONE CLAUSE. THE CLUE IS THE BLANK MONTH PAGE. Line 1 is the header " Mo  Tu  We  Th  Fr  Sa  Su"; then the week rows of a real month - seven 3-char cells, the 1st in its own column, every date printed as "%2d." (" 1.", "17.", blanks before the month starts / after it ends); then a last line "x/k/n" (a capital letter, k = 1..5, n = a date). The answer is THAT SAME PAGE with one mark on every day: cell = the date followed by exactly one character ("17Q", or "17." if you leave the dot). THE RULE, said in one breath: "x is written on two days with exactly one day between them, k times, and the first of those is the n-th." Formally: score 1 iff the page is well formed AND the days d with x on d and on d+2 and NOT on d+1 number exactly k and the earliest is n. There is no weekday clause and no other clause: pairs may straddle a weekend or a week row. "The day between is not x" is not a second clause, it is what "one day between them" means to a kid - and it is what makes a solid stripe of x score 0. WHY v6: v5 scored 0 % for 8 Opus finals in the new 7-class / 4-round / 3-demo format, two of them with a demo spent on it; players who took the demo read "every k-th working day" or "a holiday block" and never reached the three-clause rule (pair + Mon/Tue/Wed start + blocked middle), and the kid judge scored rule_statable 2/5 asking for fewer clauses. v6 deletes the Mon/Tue/Wed clause outright and deletes the blocked-middle clause by construction (the middle day simply carries a different mark). What is left is one countable relation plus the two numbers the clue already gives. SPARSE DEMOS (lever 9): solve() now fills every day that is not part of the picture with ONE filler - the clue's dot 70 % of the time, otherwise a single letter - so the answer page has exactly two distinct marks and the x-sandwiches are the loudest thing on it; the three decoys are still in every demo (100 % of 3000: a blocked run x x x, a pair three days apart, a lone x; 99.7 % have a non-counting mark before day n, so n is never simply "the first x"). Marks cover 26-54 % of days (median 37 %). Scorer: L and S are derived from the clue page (line 0 = header, lines 1..-2 = week rows, last = x/k/n), so L = number of dated cells and S = 7 - (cells in the first week row); the answer's own header is ignored (any line with no digit is skipped) and any line containing "/" is skipped, so the clue's parameter line may be KEPT or DROPPED (house rule, 2026-09-05); the answer's row structure must still be 7-S cells, then rows of 7, then 1..7. A cell may end in any single character, so "17." (dot kept) and "17E" (filler letter) are both legal non-x marks - the grader only cares where the x's are. Returning the clue page unchanged is well formed and scores 0 (no pairs at all). WITNESS TABLE, 600 fresh clues (scratchpad time6/attack.py): clue page returned unchanged, parameter line kept or dropped 0.00 %; x on every day (the stripe) 0.00 %; solid stripe from n, best length per k, every length 2..19 0.00 %; x on n and n+2 only = THE MINIMAL PROBE 20.67 % (124/124 of the k=1 clues, 0/476 of the rest; 20.67 % again with random junk letters on the free days); ALTERNATING x . x . x from n with exactly k pairs (2k+1 marks) 100.00 % at every k - THIS IS THE RULE NOW, reported honestly: the class no longer hides anything behind the every-other-day template, it IS the every-other-day template anchored at n and counted to k; the same run with a fixed mark count and no k tuning 16-32 %; the same run ending on the last day of the month with n ignored 11.67 % (n is late-biased: max of 3 draws), starting on day 2 with n ignored 0.17 %; x next door / three apart / a week apart, k times from n, 0.00 % each; random x at density 0.10-0.80 over dots 0.0-0.5 %; a random A-Z letter on every day 0.00 %; x on day n alone 0.00 %; demo replay with the letters renamed, same (L,S,k) 5.00 %, same (L,S,k,n) 13.17 % (79 of the 600 clues were repeats of a key and all 79 won - the clue space is 2993 distinct (L,S,k,n) keys, ~1575 effective, so a 3-demo team gets ~0.1 % of items this way); the true rule 100.00 %. Shape attacks on a page with the correct marks: no header, tabs, blank lines, trailing spaces, parameter line kept before or after 100 %; one long row, one token per line, lower-case marks 0 %; a page laid out from column 0 scores exactly the S=0 clues (11 %). Scorer never raises and never returns a non-binary value on 20 000 random junk strings (worst 0.067 ms), scores 0 on empty / spaces / newlines / 0 / 1 / x / "1"*100 / a 4000-char junk string / the clue itself, and agrees with an independent re-implementation of the stated rule on 9000 mutated well-formed answers with 0 disagreements. solve() scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh seeds (640/489/484/682/705 at k=1..5), 0.3 ms average, 3.6 ms worst (v5: 94 ms / 192 ms). INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH (private): (1) the clue is a calendar page with a dot on every day plus letter/number/number, so the answer is that page with marks written on it - no demo needed. (2) day n carries x and so does day n+2. (3) THE FOOTHOLD: x on n and n+2 and nowhere else scores on the k=1 clues (20.67 %), which proves the grader reads a pattern and that k counts these little sandwiches. (4) k >= 2: keep going every other day from n until you have k sandwiches. That is the whole rule. What the demo teaches in one look is (a) the sandwich is the counted thing, (b) a run of three x's in a row does NOT count (the blocked decoy), (c) x's three apart and lone x's do not count, (d) marks before day n exist and do not count, so n really is the first sandwich. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY GIVEN UP: v5's every-other-day template ceiling of 51-58 % becomes 100 %, because the template and the rule are now the same object. The class is therefore expected to move from too_hard toward calibrated/too_easy; the levers held back, in order, are (i) name the LAST counted day too (x/k/n-m), which forces both ends, (ii) require the k sandwiches to be non-overlapping (share no day), (iii) restore a single weekday clause. Human-designed for the "everyday time and place" direction: the object is a family calendar and the measurement (count the x-gap-x sandwiches) has no name.
generate:
def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    L = r.choice([28, 29, 30, 31, 30, 31])
    S = r.randrange(7)
    x = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    k = 1 if r.random() < 0.22 else r.choice([2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5])
    F = list(range(1, L - 2 * k))       # first counted day: never day 1, room for k pairs
    i = max(r.randrange(len(F)) for _ in range(2 if k == 1 else 3))
    cs = [""] * S + ["%d." % (d + 1) for d in range(L)]   # THE BLANK PAGE: one dot per day
    while len(cs) % 7:
        cs.append("")
    o = [" ".join(w.rjust(3) for w in "Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su".split())]
    for j in range(0, len(cs), 7):
        o.append(" ".join(c.rjust(3) for c in cs[j:j + 7]).rstrip())
    o.append("%s/%d/%d" % (x, k, F[i] + 1))   # letter / how many / which one is the first
    return "\n".join(o)
